title: Holding the Line Without Losing Composure
script: Marlina: [thoughtful] You called this meeting an hour before the shipment deadline to tell me the price has changed, Pak Reza. I'd like to understand why.
Reza: Costs on our end have shifted since we signed, and continuing at the original price would put us at a loss on this order.
Marlina: [carefully] I understand costs shift. What I don't understand is why I'm hearing about it now, rather than a week ago when you first knew.
Reza: I kept hoping the numbers would resolve themselves without needing this conversation at all, which, in hindsight, was simply avoidance dressed up as optimism.
Marlina: [reflective] I could raise my voice right now, and frankly, some part of me would enjoy it, but it wouldn't get my shipment out any faster.
Reza: I half expected you to walk out of this meeting, honestly. Most clients in your position would have.
Marlina: [honestly] I've considered it. But anger tends to be an expensive indulgence, and I'd rather spend that energy solving the actual problem in front of us.
Reza: What would solving it look like, from where you're sitting?
Marlina: [gently] Either you honor the original price for this order and renegotiate future ones properly, or you absorb half the difference and we split the discomfort.
Reza: The second option is fair, more than fair, given that this delay is entirely of my own making.
Marlina: [calmly] It is fair, and I want to be clear that agreeing to it isn't the same as forgetting how this was handled.
Reza: Understood. And for what it's worth, I should have brought this to you the moment I saw the numbers shifting, not the night before delivery.
Marlina: [encouraging] I appreciate you saying that plainly. Composure isn't the same as having no objection, Pak Reza, it's simply choosing when and how to raise it.
Reza: Noted, and I won't test that composure again if I can help it.
Marlina: [seriously] See that you don't. I'm patient, not infinite.

quiz.question: Why did Reza call the meeting so close to the shipment deadline?
options: To confirm the shipment was on schedule
To cancel the order entirely
To introduce a new supplier
To tell Marlina the price has changed
quiz.explanation: Reza called the meeting an hour before the deadline to tell Marlina the price had changed.

quiz.question: Why does Marlina say she doesn't raise her voice, even though part of her wants to?
options: She is afraid of losing the client relationship
She never gets angry about anything
Reza asked her to stay calm
Anger wouldn't get her shipment out any faster
quiz.explanation: She says raising her voice wouldn't get the shipment out any faster, calling anger an expensive indulgence.

quiz.question: Why didn't Reza raise the price issue a week earlier?
options: He didn't know about it until the meeting
He kept hoping the numbers would resolve themselves, which he admits was avoidance dressed up as optimism
He was on vacation
He forgot about the shipment
quiz.explanation: Reza admits he hoped the numbers would resolve themselves, which was avoidance dressed up as optimism.

quiz.question: What two options does Marlina offer Reza?
options: Cancel the contract or double the order
Switch suppliers immediately or pay full price forever
Delay the shipment indefinitely or lose the client
Honor the original price and renegotiate properly later, or absorb half the difference now
quiz.explanation: She offers either honoring the original price and renegotiating future orders properly, or absorbing half the difference now.

quiz.question: How does Marlina describe composure at the end of the conversation?
options: Choosing when and how to raise an objection, not the absence of one
The same as having no objection at all
A sign of weakness in negotiation
Something that means forgetting the incident
quiz.explanation: She says composure isn't the same as having no objection, but simply choosing when and how to raise it.

quiz.question: Why does Marlina decline the emotional satisfaction of raising her voice?
options: Later inconvenience cannot convert a commitment into an optional plan.
Reputation protection causes the narrator to damage an innocent colleague.
Anger would consume energy without solving the shipment problem.
He called passive tolerance patience while deadlines repeatedly failed.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the speaker's reasoning: Anger would consume energy without solving the shipment problem.

quiz.question: What admission reveals Reza's optimism as avoidance?
options: Keeping a promise unwillingly differs from valuing the promise despite cost.
Performed modesty had coexisted with fragile confidence and inflated competence.
He delayed disclosure despite knowing the costs had changed.
It tolerates difficulty while deliberately moving toward resolution.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the speaker's reasoning: He delayed disclosure despite knowing the costs had changed.

quiz.question: How do Marlina's alternatives allocate responsibility for the late change?
options: Reza must honour the price or absorb half the resulting loss.
She expects sufficient inconvenience to make most promises disappear.
It is an accurate public account of one's limitations.
It tests whether waiting benefits improvement or merely postpones discomfort.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the speaker's reasoning: Reza must honour the price or absorb half the resulting loss.

quiz.question: Why does accepting the compromise not restore full trust?
options: Career inconvenience carries less weight than freely given commitment.
A fair solution does not erase the supplier's poor handling.
It shows that competence can survive honest admission of error.
Their anxiety and confrontation contrast with passivity's quiet appearance.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the speaker's reasoning: A fair solution does not erase the supplier's poor handling.

quiz.question: What account of composure emerges from Marlina's conduct?
options: Commitment becomes morally meaningful when circumstances make it costly.
Protecting reputation and protecting truth often demand different responses.
Self-control shapes how objections are raised rather than eliminating them.
The behaviour is probably avoidance rather than patience.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the speaker's reasoning: Self-control shapes how objections are raised rather than eliminating them.
